newsitem.title: GERMANY: German publisher overjoyed at Pole winning Nobel.
newsitem.headline: German publisher overjoyed at Pole winning Nobel.

text.p: The German publisher of Poland's Nobel prize-winning poet Wislawa Szymborka said on Thursday he was overjoyed by the award which provoked scenes of jubilation at his Frankfurt book fair stand.

"I am overjoyed. I only heard the news 10 minutes ago and I am very, very surprised," said Dr Rainer Weiss, editor-in-chief of Suhrkamp , whose stand at the world's biggest book fair was immediately swamped with well-wishers.

"We never expected this," he told Reuters. "We have 10 to 12 Polish writers that we have been publishing for 20 years. This is a great feeling for us and a very important moment for Polish literature," he said.

Weiss said the award, that left him facing a bevy of reporters in a state of delighted shock, was certain to give a big boost to sales of the 73-year-old poet's works which Suhrkamp had been publishing since 1973.
Visitors at the firm's book fair stand clambered for copies of her poems within minutes of the award being announced.
International publishers were also very surprised that the Nobel committee had chosen a poet for the prestigious literature prize two years in a row.
The 1995 award went to Irish poet Seamus Heaney who had been in Frankfurt for the book fair opening but had ironically left for Poland when the 1996 winner of the $1.2 million prize was announced.
Heaney was on a walking tour in Greece when news of his prize was given last year.
His family and publishers failed to track him down in 24 hours of frantic phone calls and he only learnt the news when phoning home to his son in Dublin.
The reclusive Szymborska was also said to be away on a holiday in the mountains when news of her award broke.
Jonathan Galassi, president of the Academy of American Poets, said of the surprise choice: "This is wonderful news. She is the greatest living author in Poland. It is fabulous.
"With Seamus Heaney winning last year and now her, it is incredible to have two poets in a row."

U.S. publisher Roger Strauss, who publishes 20 Nobel prizewinners, said: "I would have bet anything it wouldn't have been another poet. This is a big pat on the back for the whole cultural renaissance in Poland."
